curated_comment: Ilongot has ergative-absolutive alignment (Philippine focus system). NOM marker ma marks absolutive NPs (patient of transitive + S of intransitive). Liao (2008:3) ex.(4): kinan ni Madiya ma manok = ate GEN.Maria NOM.chicken ("Maria ate the chicken"). ma is overt ABS marker.

GEN pronoun =ko (1sg agent) vs NOM =/(C)ak (1sg S/O). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1 and §4.2.2: NOM pronoun functions as S of intransitive (ex.14), agent of dyadic intransitive (ex.15), AND theme/patient of transitive (ex.16). GEN =ko marks transitive agent. Ergative alignment on 1sg.
GEN pronoun =mo (2sg agent) vs NOM =ka (2sg S/O). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1 and §4.2.2. Same pattern as 1sg. Ergative alignment on 2sg.

GEN pronoun =to/=tu (3sg agent) vs no NOM 3sg form (zero/absent). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1: 3sg NOM is "---" (no form). Ex.(16): kadɨvaan=tu=(v)ak (accompany=GEN.3SG=NOM.1SG) "She will accompany me" — 3sg agent uses GEN. Ergative alignment present on 3sg (agent marked by GEN).

Full NP: ni (GEN, agent marker) vs ma (NOM, patient/S marker). Liao (2008:3) ex.(4): kinan ni Madiya ma manok noy mase (ate GEN.Maria NOM.chicken last.night) "Maria ate the chicken last night." Overt ergative-absolutive alignment on full NPs.

Liao (2008) is a 10-page preliminary study covering only word order and pronoun forms. Insufficient data to code aspect/tense/mood/agentivity conditioning of ERG alignment. Note: GB409_1-5=1 and GB409_23=1 are confirmed. Further grammatical description needed.

ERG=GEN: The ergative/agent marker IS the genitive marker in Ilongot. Liao (2008:4) §4.2.1: "the genitive pronoun in Ilongot is used as a nominal modifier AND as the agent of a transitive clause." Full NP: ni is both genitive and agent marker. Pronoun series: GEN (=ko, =mo, =to etc.) functions both as possessive and transitive agent.
